PullRequest.Title: Add usage telemetry to the Markdown Editor
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #348910

The Markdown Editor (the `vscode.markdown.editor` custom editor) sent no usage telemetry, so we could not tell whether people read or edit with it, how long they use it, or whether they leave it right away. This PR adds a summary event per editor session and an event per read/edit switch. No content, file names or paths are reported.

## Events

**`markdownEditor.session`**: sent once per editor (webview panel) when it is closed, or when the extension deactivates because the window closes or reloads.

| Field | Kind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionId` | property | Random id per session |
| `scheme` | property | `file`, `untitled` or `other` |
| `sizeBucket` | property | Document length in characters when opened: `0`, `<1k`, `<10k`, `<100k`, `>=100k` |
| `initialMode`, `finalMode` | property | `read` or `edit` |
| `ended` | property | `closed` (editor closed, or reopened with another editor; both dispose the panel and cannot be told apart) or `shutdown` |
| `untitledDocumentId` | property | Only for untitled documents: the id of the workbench's `untitledDocument` events |
| `modeSwitches` | measurement | Number of read/edit switches |
| `editCount` | measurement | Document changes made through this editor: typing/formatting in the webview, plus rename, completion acceptance and media paste (not changes through other editors of the same document) |
| `firstEditMs` | measurement | Time from opening to the first such change, `-1` if none |
| `visibleMs` | measurement | Time the editor was visible |
| `focusedMs` | measurement | Time the editor was visible, the active editor, and in a focused window |
| `lifetimeMs` | measurement | Time from opening to the end of the session |

**`markdownEditor.modeChanged`**: `sessionId`, `to` (`read`/`edit`), measurement `msSinceOpen`.

Inline diff editors that use the Markdown Editor are not counted as sessions. Both events carry `__GDPR__` annotations.

## Implementation

- `MarkdownEditorSessionTelemetry` (`src/preview/markdownEditorTelemetry.ts`) is a small state machine with an injectable clock; the provider feeds it mode switches (`setReadonly`), applied webview edits, and panel/window view-state changes, and ends it on panel dispose. Both entry points export `deactivate`, which ends the open sessions as `shutdown` and awaits the reporter's flush; the extension host awaits it on window close and reload. As a fallback the reporter is disposed after the provider.
- **Fix:** `loadDefaultTelemetryReporter` looked up the extension by its old id `Microsoft.vscode-markdown`, which no longer exists, so it always fell back to a no-op reporter and the extension's existing `openPreview` event was never sent either. It now reads the `aiKey` from `context.extension`. As a side effect, `openPreview` is sent again.
- Core gets an internal `_workbench.getUntitledDocumentId` command (`files.contribution.ts`) so the Markdown Editor can link its sessions to the untitled document funnel.

## Limitations

- `shutdown` relies on extension deactivation on window close/reload. If the extension host is killed (crash, forced quit) or deactivation times out, the session event is lost.
- `editCount` counts applied edits, roughly one per keystroke or formatting action, not "edit sessions".

## Validation

- New unit tests `src/test/markdownEditorTelemetry.test.ts` (mode switches, edits, visible/focused time with a fake clock, untitled + shutdown).
- Markdown extension integration tests: 217 passing.
- Markdown tsconfig type checks and the workbench type check (`src/tsconfig.json`) pass; `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files is clean.
- Manually in Code OSS with the telemetry log at Trace:
  - `.md` file opened in the Markdown Editor, switched read → edit, typed, hidden behind another editor for ~3 s, saved, closed: two `markdownEditor.modeChanged` events and a `markdownEditor.session` with `ended: closed`, `modeSwitches: 2`, `editCount` matching the typed characters, and `visibleMs` about 3 s below `lifetimeMs`.
  - A session whose only change was a heading rename (F2 in the Markdown Editor): `editCount: 1`.
  - New untitled file reopened in the Markdown Editor, typed, window reloaded: `markdownEditor.session` with `scheme: untitled`, `ended: shutdown`, and an `untitledDocumentId` that matches the core `untitledDocument` events of that document.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate Markdown language features in desktop or browser, including opening ordinary Markdown without using the custom editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Both entry points await the existing language-client startup before activateShared constructs one telemetry reporter and registers providers. The diff enables the real reporter by reading the current extension's aiKey; it does not add another language-server startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the existing desktop language server using IPC transport, or the existing browser Worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One language client/server per extension activation, not per telemetry session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical server/Worker startup and awaiting order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Client startup is awaited before activateShared in both versions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct @vscode/extension-telemetry with the configured key; SDK initialization and subsequent transport are delegated to that dependency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared SDK reporter per activation. Internal initialization requests and transport batching cannot be established from the available repository snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The obsolete extension-id lookup normally selected nullReporter, so the real SDK reporter was not constructed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter construction occurs synchronously within activateShared; the diff adds no awaited network operation during activation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One reporter per extension activation, regardless of document or panel count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing one-server activation sequence; one reporter construction. SDK-internal concurrency is unavailable for inspection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reporter is shared by previews and all custom-editor sessions, rather than initialized per document. No added document-keyed initialization cache or repeated failure retry exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the activation call path and singleton cardinality. No evidence establishes heavyweight repeated initialization, new subprocess fan-out, or an avoidable blocking network dependency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK implementation is not present in the accessible dependency path, so initialization cost and networking details remain unverified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: real telemetry is intentionally enabled once, with no demonstrated pathological initialization mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore file-backed and untitled custom Markdown editors, including multiple panels for one document and inline diffs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: #wireSingle reads document text, creates session accounting for non-diff panels, wires handlers, and configures webview HTML. The new untitled-id command is dispatched without awaiting its result, so rendering does not wait for the command round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send an untitled document URI to the main-thread command and return its existing telemetry id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command RPC per untitled non-diff panel opening; U requests for U such panels. No retries or additional filesystem/database operations are added by the handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No untitled telemetry-id lookup from the custom editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the rendering critical path: the returned promise only updates the session id metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode document content into initial webview state and assign webview HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing full-content initial-state serialization per panel. The new text-length read does not encode or send content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical initial document serialization and webview configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before rendering the editor in both versions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P non-diff panels, U of them untitled; document length L. Sessions are per panel, including split panels, not deduplicated by URI. Inline diff panels add no session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Panel setup is synchronous within each #wireSingle invocation. Untitled lookup promises may overlap across opening panels; no per-panel network send is made at session creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ExtHostDocumentData.document.getText delegates to MirrorTextModel.getText, which caches the joined document string. #wireSingle already calls getText before the newly added getText().length; there is no intervening await or mutation. Consequently the added length read is warm even on a cold editor open. The untitled service is already eagerly created at BlockStartup, and getUntitledDocumentId is an existing ResourceMap lookup; misses do not schedule retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the text cache, call ordering, command RPC, already-eager service ownership, and constant-time lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large restored panel counts affect the number of small command RPCs, but no document-size-dependent additional copy or rendering-blocking lookup was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: suspected extra full-document allocation is ruled out by the existing cache, and the sole added IPC is a small off-path lookup per untitled panel.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, format, rename, accept completions, and paste media through a Markdown editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Typing retains the existing RecoveringTaskQueue and awaited workspace edit. Rename/completion/media handlers retain their existing drain, validation, provider and apply sequence. The new wrapper awaits the same applyEdit once and then updates in-memory telemetry counters.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize a WorkspaceEdit and invoke main-thread $tryApplyWorkspaceEdit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing apply IPC per accepted typing operation, rename, completion acceptance, or media-paste action. Multi-resource edits remain grouped in the same WorkspaceEdit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same applyEdit calls with the same edit payloads; rename/completion/media used their default API delegates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the corresponding action completes, unchanged by the diff apart from constant-size bookkeeping afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute rename/completion provider commands and an optional completion follow-up command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Rename retains one prepare and one rename-provider request. Completion retains one listing request and a fresh resolving request on acceptance, plus an optional follow-up command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same command delegates and request cardinalities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited provider commands remain on the action critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Choose destination paths, materialize clipboard media through renderer calls, and create media files using the grouped additionalEdits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing path generation per media entry, clipboard reads scaling with media bytes/chunks, and up to M file creations in one applyEdit. No extra reads or writes are added by the telemetry wrapper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical preparation and file-creation path using the default apply delegate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Media preparation and grouped edit application were already awaited before paste completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E successful edit operations; rename may affect R resources in one WorkspaceEdit; a media paste may contain M files and B bytes. Telemetry counts operations, not individual resource edits or bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Typing edits are serialized per panel by RecoveringTaskQueue, not globally across panels. Existing rename/completion in-progress guards and media cancellation remain. Media path generation uses Promise.all; materialization iterates entries before one grouped edit. Telemetry adds no tasks or transport per keystroke.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing document/snapshot caching and completion/rename session validation are unchanged. recordEdit retains only a count and the first-edit timestamp, not edit text, WorkspaceEdits, provider results, or a growing edit history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected API defaults, injected wrappers, queue implementation, media preparation, and main-thread bulk-edit boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying rename workspace size and media bytes can be large, but those costs and their concurrency are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no additional expensive boundary calls, full edit clones, or per-keystroke telemetry events are introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch read/edit mode, change panel visibility, focus the window, and repeatedly open and close Markdown editors.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mode switches add one constant-size sendTelemetryEvent before the existing globalState.update. Focus/visibility notifications update timestamps synchronously without timers or renderer calls. Closing a panel disposes both new listeners, removes its session from the provider Set, and sends one summary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit bounded mode-change and session-summary records to the shared telemetry SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: S mode-change submissions and C session-summary submissions. Same-mode assignments are suppressed, and end is idempotent. Exact HTTP request count depends on SDK batching and telemetry enablement; it is not assumed to be one request per event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No custom-editor mode/session telemetry was submitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No network promise is awaited for mode switches or panel close; synchronous event payload construction is constant-size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected read/edit mode and update existing editor-focus context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing state update per setReadonly message and existing context updates on relevant focus changes; telemetry adds no calls to either.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same persistence and context operations without timestamp/counter accounting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing mode persistence is still awaited. Added focus accounting performs no boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P currently open non-diff panels, S actual mode changes, and C closed sessions. Window-state notifications visit P registered callbacks; retained session objects and listeners are O(P), not O(total historical opens or edits).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Callbacks run synchronously in the extension host; one shared reporter handles event submissions. Independent panels can submit events, but no new per-event subprocess or await chain is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mode deduplication and the ended flag prevent redundant events. Session removal and listener disposal occur in the panel's existing disposal handler. No polling, growing timestamp list, or content retention was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: session state, guards, listener ownership, disposal call site, and before/after handler behavior were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK transport batching is unavailable; the extension-side event cardinality and fixed payload bounds are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: state is bounded by live panels, edit traffic is summarized, and event emission has explicit deduplication.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open ordinary Markdown previews, including a multi-selection preview command.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: showPreview resolves the resource and invokes openDynamicPreview before submitting openPreview telemetry. Enabling the real reporter restores this existing event call; it does not add an await before preview creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the existing two-property openPreview event through the now-enabled SDK reporter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded event submission per valid resource/action, including K submissions for K selected resources. HTTP batching and request counts are SDK-owned and unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sendTelemetryEvent call normally reached nullReporter because of the obsolete extension-id lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Submission follows preview opening and is not awaited.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K valid resources passed to ShowPreviewCommand, or one resource for a side/locked-preview action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing multi-resource command invokes showPreview for each resource without awaiting; telemetry does not alter this scheduling or add a new per-resource heavyweight request that is established by the available source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All previews reuse the activation-scoped reporter. No per-resource reporter allocation, content serialization, telemetry history cache, or negative-cache retry is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in event placement, bounded payload, and shared reporter ownership; no evidence of a concrete inefficient transport fan-out mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-selection prevalence and SDK packet batching are unknown; event payloads and producer cardinality are fixed and visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this enables intentionally bounded usage events on the existing user-action path, with no demonstrated repeated expensive computation or blocking network operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close or reload the window with custom Markdown editors still open, or dispose extension subscriptions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new deactivate hook synchronously ends all live sessions and awaits one reporter-disposal promise. The host starts deactivation for activated extensions in parallel and caps extension-host termination at five seconds. Subscription disposal is invoked immediately after starting a module's deactivate, rather than waiting for its promise; the reporter's memoized disposal and ended guards cover the overlapping cleanup calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit up to P session summaries, then ask the shared telemetry SDK to dispose/flush.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One summary per previously unended live panel and one underlying reporter.dispose invocation. Subsequent provider or subscription cleanup reuses the same promise and emits no duplicate summaries. Exact flush transport requests are SDK-owned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No custom-editor session summaries or exported asynchronous deactivation hook; reporter disposal was a subscription cleanup call, normally on the no-op reporter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new deactivate promise participates in host shutdown, subject to the existing five-second host limit; regular editing and panel closure do not await this flush.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P live custom-editor sessions at shutdown, plus already-buffered bounded telemetry events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session payloads are submitted in one synchronous loop over live panels, followed by one SDK disposal promise. The host uses Promise.all for extension deactivations, not a serial per-editor or per-extension network wait.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: end marks sessions ended before submission and clears the Set. ExtensionReporter caches #disposed so concurrent or later disposal does not re-flush. No history-sized synchronous traversal or document-content serialization occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High in shutdown reachability, P-session cardinality, idempotence, overlapping subscription cleanup, and host-level concurrency/timeout. No high-confidence pathological network-delay mechanism can be inferred solely from calling dispose.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK flush latency, offline behavior, and batching could not be inspected because dependency implementation is unavailable. The changed scheduling is explicit and intentional; no independent repeated-flush or unbounded-serialization mechanism was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: awaiting delivery is an explicit lifecycle tradeoff, bounded by existing host termination policy, with correct event/disposal coalescing and no demonstrated amplified cleanup work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 11 changed files and every diff page against base 4138d130b9f47e7343ea3904a1b20f1e602ac344. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance bug or concrete performance-regression fix was found. Rejected extra-text-copy concern using the actual MirrorTextModel cache; verified constant-size edit accounting, per-panel listener/session cleanup, event deduplication, unchanged grouped workspace-edit and media boundaries, non-awaited untitled lookup, and memoized shutdown disposal. Review limitation: third-party telemetry SDK initialization, batching, and flush internals were not available in the repository snapshot.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
